title: Best OpenClaw Skills for Job Search in 2026: Apply, Tailor and Track
summary: ClawHub has dozens of job skills. Tsenta ranks 2026’s best OpenClaw skills for finding jobs, tailoring résumés, tracking applications and applying.
body_markdown:
**The best OpenClaw skills for job search in 2026 are JobAppAgent, ApplySent and Tolta for applying, Job Search (JobSpy MCP) and openclaw-jobsearch for finding roles, Resume / CV Builder and resume-tailor for your résumé, and Job Hunt Tracker and Job Search Tracker for tracking.** Yes, an OpenClaw skill can apply to jobs for you, mostly by driving a browser on the application form or by connecting OpenClaw to a service that submits, and a few email your résumé to employers from your Gmail. “Job Auto Apply,” the most-downloaded auto-apply skill we found on ClawHub, submits nothing: its script is a placeholder.


Tsenta is not a skill. It is an MCP server that connects your own AI assistant to your Tsenta account, so the assistant can find roles, tailor your résumé for each one and start applications that Tsenta submits on supported company career sites. OpenClaw can add remote MCP servers with OAuth sign-in, but Tsenta has no OpenClaw guide yet. Setup for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Codex is at[tsenta.com/mcp](https://tsenta.com/mcp) .


Checked November 20, 2026. Tsenta publishes this guide and sells one of the services in it. We read each skill’s SKILL.md or README, ClawHub’s registry data and OpenClaw’s docs that day, and did not run the skills. Download counts are ClawHub’s counters, not users. Within each group, the order favors documented behavior, recent releases, your control and setup effort.


## How an OpenClaw skill applies to jobs


[OpenClaw’s docs](https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/skills) define skills as “markdown instruction files that teach the agent how and when to use tools,” so a skill only uses tools your agent already has. A job skill that “applies” usually **drives a browser** on your machine with your logins, or **calls a service’s MCP server** , such as ApplySent’s or Tolta’s, and the service submits. A few email your résumé to employers from your Gmail instead. You add a server with` openclaw mcp set` and sign in with` openclaw mcp login` , as[OpenClaw’s MCP docs](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/mcp/transports) describe. An MCP server also works with no skill at all, which is how Tsenta connects.

## Skills and MCP servers that apply to jobs


### 1. Tsenta: an MCP server rather than an OpenClaw skill


Tsenta watches 300,000+ company career pages. Through its MCP server, your assistant can get roles ranked against your profile, read job descriptions and links you paste, and start applications that Tsenta submits in the cloud on supported company career sites. Tsenta tailors your résumé for each role in Honest or Aggressive mode, or sends it as written, and drafts a cover letter when the form takes one. The same account keeps your tracker and a Tsenta inbox for recruiter replies.


**Connecting it to OpenClaw.** Tsenta connects to OpenClaw as an MCP server rather than a skill, and it has no ClawHub listing.[OpenClaw’s docs](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/mcp/transports) describe saving a remote server with the streamable-http transport and OAuth, then signing in with` openclaw mcp login` . Use Tsenta’s server address,` https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp` , there. Set the transport to streamable-http, because OpenClaw uses SSE when it is left out. Tsenta does not publish a step-by-step OpenClaw guide yet, so check the tools OpenClaw lists after you sign in. Set your address and location in the Tsenta dashboard first, because your assistant cannot. The[Help Center guide](https://help.tsenta.com/connect-claude-chatgpt-mcp) covers privacy and disconnecting.


**Limits.** One approval gives the assistant every available Tsenta tool on your account, including tools that edit your profile and reply to emails. Whether OpenClaw asks before each action depends on your OpenClaw settings, not on Tsenta. OpenClaw’s MCP sign-ins are shared by default, so on a Gateway other people message, set` oauth.identity` to` per-requester` . With résumé auto-approval off, each tailored résumé waits for you, and form review stops before the final submit on employer systems that support pausing. Auto Apply, which submits eligible roles without per-role approval, needs Power; on Starter and Pro you choose each role and Tsenta submits it.


**Price.** The first 25 applications are free, with no card. In USD global pricing, Starter is $19 a month for 600 applications, Pro $39 for 1,500 and Power $99 for 4,500 per 30-day cycle. See[pricing](https://tsenta.com/pricing) .


**Where others win.** ApplySent and Tolta publish ClawHub skills, and JobAppAgent is free and open source. For Claude setup, see the[Claude connector page](https://tsenta.com/connectors/claude) or our[guide to connecting a job search agent to Claude or ChatGPT](https://tsenta.com/blog/connect-ai-job-search-agent-to-claude-chatgpt-2026) .


### 2. JobAppAgent: open-source applying from your own browser


[JobAppAgent](https://github.com/vaibhavarora14/job-application-agent) finds and scores roles against one verified résumé, fills the application on the employer’s own page and records only submissions the site confirms. Its default` review-each` mode stops before Submit; an opt-in` routine-auto` grant submits without asking each time. It pauses for passwords, SSO, MFA, CAPTCHAs, legal attestations and unclear work authorization or sponsorship.


```text
openclaw skills install @vaibhavarora14/job-application-agent


```


Or run its installer,` npx job-application-agent@latest install` , which puts it in` ~/.agents/skills` , a folder OpenClaw loads.


**Limits.** Its README limits applying to a short list of named applicant tracking systems. Usage analytics, anonymous community sharing and contact sharing, which stores your saved name and email with the maintainer, are on by default;` telemetry disable` stops analytics and contact sharing. It runs on your machine, and a hosted version is not live yet. **Where it wins:** free under MIT, 177 GitHub stars, updated November 20, 2026.


### 3. ApplySent: one approved application at a time


[ApplySent’s skill](https://clawhub.ai/applysent/skills/applysent) connects OpenClaw to ApplySent’s hosted MCP server. Your assistant can search jobs that fit your résumé, preview a tailored résumé that “only rewrites facts already in the user’s résumé” and apply on the employer’s own form. Through the skill, each application needs its own yes, confirmed with a single-use token that expires after 10 minutes, and the skill says “There is no bulk or automatic applying.” ApplySent’s own app also offers an optional Autopilot mode, per[its pricing page](https://applysent.com/pricing) .


```text
openclaw skills install @applysent/applysent


```


Then add` https://applysent.com/api/mcp` as a Streamable HTTP server with OAuth, the same way as Tolta’s commands below. ApplySent gives the address but no OpenClaw command.


**Limits.** It does not apply through LinkedIn Easy Apply or Indeed, only on the hiring systems ApplySent lists.[Its pricing page](https://applysent.com/pricing) showed $19.99 a month for up to 750 applications, or $49.99 every 3 months, with a 7-day trial that needs a card, as of November 20, 2026.


### 4. Tolta: apply to today’s matches from chat


[Tolta’s skill](https://clawhub.ai/wassim/skills/tolta) prints the exact OpenClaw commands for its server. Install the skill, then run Tolta’s two commands:


```text
openclaw skills install @wassim/tolta
openclaw mcp set tolta '{"url":"https://tolta.ai/mcp","transport":"streamable-http","auth":"oauth"}'
openclaw mcp login tolta


```


Tolta matches roles from company career boards to your profile, tailors your CV and applies on the employer’s own form. From chat, your assistant can list today’s matches with a fit score out of 100, search jobs, read applications and call` apply_to_match` , which “sends a real application (or a draft to review, if the user reviews applications in Tolta).”


**Limits.** Only today’s matches can be applied to from chat, and you answer application questions in Tolta. “During the trial the tools can read matches, jobs and applications but can’t apply.”[Tolta’s pricing page](https://tolta.ai/pricing) listed $19.99 a week for 50 applications, $39.99 a month for 200 and $79.99 every 3 months for 600, as of November 20, 2026.


### 5. Job Apply Pilot: one job link, checked before Submit


[Job Apply Pilot](https://github.com/bobothebest007/job-apply-pilot) is “a workflow skill, not a standalone auto-apply service.” Give it one job URL, and it checks for a duplicate, reviews the whole form, asks about anything it cannot verify, submits once and logs the application only after the site confirms it. Its README says to copy` SKILL.md` into` <workspace>/skills/job-apply-pilot/` ; with` SKILL.md` at the repository root, this should also work (not tested):


```text
openclaw skills install git:bobothebest007/job-apply-pilot


```


**Limits.** It “does not include a résumé, credentials, a tracker, or a browser extension” and “does not bypass captchas, login challenges, or access restrictions.” It has one commit and no stars.


### 6. Job Autopilot: search, tailor and submit in OpenClaw’s browser


[Job Autopilot](https://clawhub.ai/jerronl/skills/jobautopilot-bundle) bundles three skills. Search uses LinkedIn Jobs as its primary source, plus company career pages. Tailor rewrites your résumé and cover letter. The submitter fills multi-step forms, uploads your tailored résumé and cover letter and “confirms successful submission” through the` openclaw browser` CLI.


```text
openclaw skills install @jerronl/jobautopilot-bundle


```


The bundle’s` install.sh` adds the three skills, and` setup.sh` saves your name, email, phone and LinkedIn URL to a local config file. **Limits.** The submitter describes no approval step before each submission, and you sign in to sites by hand. For how browser agents and hosted services differ, see[how AI agents apply to jobs](https://tsenta.com/blog/how-ai-agents-apply-to-jobs-2026) .


## Job search skills


### 7. Job Search (JobSpy MCP): search the big boards


[Job Search](https://clawhub.ai/amoghpurohit/skills/job-search-mcp) teaches OpenClaw to use the open-source JobSpy MCP server to search LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter, Google Jobs, Bayt, Naukri and BDJobs by keyword, location, job type, remote work and posting age.[LobeHub lists the same file](https://lobehub.com/skills/openclaw-skills-job-search-mcp) as “Job Search MCP.”


```text
openclaw skills install @amoghpurohit/job-search-mcp


```


**Limits.** You run the JobSpy MCP server yourself with Python 3.10 or newer, and its setup examples are written for Claude Desktop. The skill keeps LinkedIn to 10 to 15 results because LinkedIn is rate limited, and LobeHub’s one review says searches were “blocked by Cloudflare/CAPTCHA on OCC, Indeed, and Google.” Its` easy_apply` option is only a search filter.


### 8. openclaw-jobsearch: rank one employer’s open roles


[openclaw-jobsearch](https://github.com/jordmorr/openclaw-jobsearch) ranks “live job listings from a single employer’s careers portal” against your profile. Name an employer, and it finds the careers site in` EMPLOYERS.yaml` (105 employers, from big tech and frontier AI to quantum computing), filters roles with` PREFERENCES.md` , scores them against` USER.md` and returns up to 10 with fit scores, risks and links. It must not invent visa support or pay.


The README has no install command, and` SKILL.md` sits in a subfolder, so a` git:` install will not find it. Clone it and install the folder (not tested), then put` EMPLOYERS.yaml` and your own` PREFERENCES.md` in your workspace (` ~/.openclaw/workspace` by default):


```text
git clone https://github.com/jordmorr/openclaw-jobsearch
openclaw skills install ./openclaw-jobsearch/skills/openclaw-jobsearch


```


**Limits.** One employer per run and no application step. Results can be incomplete when a careers site leans on JavaScript or blocks browsing, and the sample preferences are the author’s own.


### 9. Remote Jobs Finder: Remote Rocketship’s remote feed


[Remote Rocketship’s OpenClaw page](https://www.remoterocketship.com/openclaw/) pairs its skill with a gateway extension that returns 20 remote jobs per call by default, up to 50, and can check for new jobs on a schedule.


```text
openclaw skills install @lior539/remote-jobs-finder


```


**Limits.** You also copy two extension files into` ~/.openclaw/extensions` , enable them in` openclaw.json` and set` RR_API_KEY` on the Gateway service. “The job feed is a paid Remote Rocketship feature.” Remote roles only, and it does not apply.


**Indeed’s official plugin.** We found no official OpenClaw job search skill. OpenClaw’s official plugins on ClawHub include the` @openclaw/indeed`[plugin](https://clawhub.ai/openclaw/plugins/indeed) , which wraps Indeed’s own MCP server to search Indeed listings. Install it with` openclaw plugins install clawhub:@openclaw/indeed` . It does not apply.


## Résumé tailoring skills


### 10. Resume / CV Builder: writing guidance and export


[Resume / CV Builder](https://clawhub.ai/sebastian-buitrag0/skills/resume-cv-builder) has 5,628 ClawHub downloads. It sets out to “optimize bullet points, tailor for specific jobs, and export to multiple formats,” with sample résumés for software, product and marketing roles.


```text
openclaw skills install @sebastian-buitrag0/resume-cv-builder


```


**Limits.** It is mostly writing guidance and templates, it needs` pandoc` for exports, and its homepage field is a placeholder. Its “ATS-friendly” label does not promise that an employer’s system reads the file well.


**A more downloaded alternative.**[Resume Assistant](https://clawhub.ai/wscats/skills/resume-assistant) (` @wscats/resume-assistant` ) has 22,027 downloads, the most of any résumé skill we found on ClawHub, and its last release was March 14, 2026. It polishes your résumé, tailors it to a job description with a gap table, scores it out of 100 and exports it in several formats. Its tailoring prompt tells the agent to add metrics where a bullet has none, so check every number before you send it.


### 11. resume-tailor: one job description in, one .docx out


[resume-tailor](https://github.com/lqminhhh/openclaw-resume-tailor) takes your résumé (PDF, DOCX, TEX, TXT or MD) and a job description, tailors it “without inventing facts” and saves one` .docx` . In chat it returns only the file path, strengths, gaps and improvements, and it never overwrites your original.


```text
git clone https://github.com/lqminhhh/openclaw-resume-tailor
openclaw skills install ./openclaw-resume-tailor


```


**Limits.** It needs Python for its scripts, the repository has no license, and the last commit was March 28, 2026. On ClawHub,` @ivangdavila/resume` and` @suntianchong/resume-tailor` , which adds a cover letter, are alternatives. To compare tailoring in other assistants, see[résumé tailoring connectors by assistant](https://tsenta.com/blog/ai-assistant-connectors-tailor-resume-2026) .


## Job-hunt tracker skills


These skills keep a record on your machine or in your own Notion, filled by you or from your email. Services that submit for you track their own applications: Tsenta’s tracker holds every application Tsenta submits plus roles you add from elsewhere, in Applied, Interviewing, Offer, Rejected and Ghosted stages. See[tracking job applications with AI assistants](https://tsenta.com/blog/track-job-applications-ai-assistants-2026) for options outside OpenClaw.


### 12. Job Hunt Tracker: a local pipeline with reminders


[Job Hunt Tracker](https://clawhub.ai/mkpareek0315/skills/job-hunt-tracker) is a “20-feature AI job hunt tracker with application pipeline, interview scheduler, offer comparator, follow-up reminders, rejection analyzer, and job search gamification.” It stores JSON files under` ~/.openclaw/job-hunt-tracker/` and makes “NO external API calls.”


```text
openclaw skills install @mkpareek0315/job-hunt-tracker


```


**Limits.** You log each application yourself, and its examples lean toward India, with salaries in lakhs per annum.


### 13. Job Search Tracker: one markdown file and follow-up drafts


[Job Search Tracker](https://clawhub.ai/chris/skills/job-search-tracker) keeps applications in` applications.md` in your working folder, flags stale ones and drafts follow-ups, cover letters and thank-you notes. With Gmail, LinkedIn or browser tools connected, it can find applications, but must show you and wait for your yes before adding them.


```text
openclaw skills install @chris/job-search-tracker


```


**Limits.** It ships no Gmail or LinkedIn tools, so those lookups depend on what you have connected.


### 14. Job Application Manager: Gmail into Notion or SQLite


[Job Application Manager](https://clawhub.ai/chenyuan99/skills/job-application-manager) scans Gmail for application emails, classifies offers, rejections and interview invitations, updates a Notion database or local SQLite file, and flags applications with no email activity for 30 days or more.


```text
openclaw skills install @chenyuan99/job-application-manager


```


**Limits.** It expects a Gmail MCP server, and a Notion one if you track in Notion, under names taken from Claude’s connectors, so connect your own in OpenClaw first. Check each status change it makes.


## Skills to skip or handle with care


**Job Auto Apply (` @veeky-kumar/job-auto-apply` ).** At 6,221 downloads, it is the most-downloaded auto-apply skill on ClawHub in our searches, and it says it applies on LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter and Wellfound. Its` job_search_apply.py` does not. The search function returns an empty list under a comment that reads “This is a placeholder,” and the apply function only prints “Application submitted successfully.”


**LinkedIn Easy Apply automation skills.**` @ralyodio/linkedin-easy-apply-automation` drives LinkedIn Easy Apply with Puppeteer, stops for CAPTCHA, MFA and suspicious-login checks, and caps its example run at 10 applications.` @umerkha2007/linkedin-easy-apply` ships no automation code of its own: it runs a separately installed runtime, and it sends connection requests to the hiring team after each submission unless you set` AUTO_CONNECT_HIRING_TEAM=false` .


## Before a skill drives a browser on a job board


A skill that submits by browser acts as you, with your logins. Check four things first.


1. **The site’s own terms.** Read the terms of every site a skill will drive before you run it.
2. **OpenClaw’s own warning.**[OpenClaw’s browser docs](https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/browser-login) say to sign in by hand, because “Automated logins often trigger anti-bot defenses and can lock the account.”
3. **What else the skill sends.** One LinkedIn skill above sends connection requests by default, and JobAppAgent shares analytics and your saved contact details unless you opt out.
4. **Who can trigger it.** OpenClaw answers in WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack and other chat apps. Its[security FAQ](https://docs.openclaw.ai/help/faq/security-and-access-control) lists the practical risks as “gateway exposure, who can message the bot, prompt injection, tool scope, credential handling, browser access, exec access, and third-party skill/plugin trust.” Keep an approval step for each application.


## How to install OpenClaw skills from ClawHub or GitHub


[ClawHub](https://clawhub.ai/) is “the public registry for OpenClaw skills and plugins.” The[OpenClaw CLI](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/skills) searches it, installs from it by owner, installs from GitHub or a local folder, and updates:


```text
openclaw skills search job
openclaw skills install @owner/slug
openclaw skills install git:owner/repo
openclaw skills install ./path/to/skill
openclaw skills update --all


```


- **Use the owner name.** Two publishers use` job-auto-apply` , and ClawHub answers a bare request with an ambiguity error.
- **GitHub installs need` SKILL.md` at the repository root.** Otherwise clone and install the folder. Run` openclaw skills list` after, and` /new` if the skill does not show.
- **Anyone can publish.**[ClawHub’s docs](https://docs.openclaw.ai/clawhub) say “anyone can upload,” with automated scans, and OpenClaw’s security FAQ says “scans are not a complete security boundary.”
- **Directories copy listings.** LobeHub, skills.lc and clawskills.sh are not run by OpenClaw. LobeHub credits Job Search MCP to “openclaw” and links github.com/openclaw/skills, which returns Not Found. Find the original publisher.


OpenClaw has[no paid tier](https://docs.openclaw.ai/) ; you pay for the AI model you connect, per[OpenClaw’s cost docs](https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/api-usage-costs) . Hosts such as[TryOpenClaw.ai](https://www.tryopenclaw.ai/use-cases/job-search-assistant/) , which[says it is not affiliated](https://www.tryopenclaw.ai/about) with the OpenClaw project, charge $39 a month after a $1 trial, as of November 20, 2026.


For other assistants, see the[best MCP servers for job search](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-mcp-servers-job-search-2026) , the[best Claude connectors for job search](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-claude-connectors-job-search-2026) and the[best Grok Bot plugins for job search](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-grok-bot-plugins-job-search-2026) .


## Frequently asked questions


### What are the best OpenClaw skills for job search?


The best OpenClaw skills for job search in 2026 are JobAppAgent, ApplySent and Tolta for applying, Job Search (JobSpy MCP) and openclaw-jobsearch for finding roles, Resume / CV Builder and resume-tailor for your résumé, and Job Hunt Tracker and Job Search Tracker for tracking. Tsenta’s MCP server connects to OpenClaw as a server rather than a skill and covers finding, tailoring, applying and tracking in one account, though Tsenta does not publish a step-by-step OpenClaw guide yet. Every one of these skills is a community listing rather than an official OpenClaw skill, so check its last release and approval rules before you install it.


### Is there an OpenClaw skill that applies to jobs for me?


Yes, some OpenClaw skills apply to jobs for you, mostly by driving a browser on the application form or by connecting OpenClaw to a service that submits, and a few email your résumé to employers from your Gmail. JobAppAgent fills the employer’s own application page and stops before Submit by default, and ApplySent and Tolta connect OpenClaw to hosted services that submit when you ask. Tsenta connects to OpenClaw as an MCP server rather than a skill, and Tsenta does not publish a step-by-step OpenClaw guide yet. Skip Job Auto Apply, the most-downloaded auto-apply skill on ClawHub in our searches, because its script is a placeholder that submits nothing.


### Which OpenClaw skills track job applications?


Job Hunt Tracker and Job Search Tracker track job applications in OpenClaw, and both keep your data in local files on your own machine. Job Application Manager syncs application emails from Gmail into Notion or SQLite once you connect a Gmail MCP server. Services you connect to OpenClaw, such as Tsenta, ApplySent and Tolta, also track the applications they submit in their own accounts.


### Where can I find job application skills in the OpenClaw skills marketplace?


ClawHub, at clawhub.ai, is OpenClaw’s public registry for skills and plugins, and running openclaw skills search job searches it from your terminal. Anyone with a GitHub account old enough to pass its upload gate can publish there, and slugs repeat across publishers, so install with the owner name, such as openclaw skills install @applysent/applysent. LobeHub, skills.lc and clawskills.sh index or copy skills but are not run by OpenClaw.


### Can I install OpenClaw skills from GitHub?


Yes, the command openclaw skills install git:owner/repo installs a skill straight from GitHub when its SKILL.md file sits at the repository root. When it sits in a subfolder, as in openclaw-jobsearch, clone the repository and install that folder with openclaw skills install ./path/to/folder. OpenClaw has no built-in dangerous-code blocking during installs, so read the SKILL.md and any scripts first.


### Which OpenClaw skills tailor a résumé to a job?


Resume / CV Builder and resume-tailor are the OpenClaw skills to start with for résumé tailoring. Resume / CV Builder, with 5,628 ClawHub downloads, rewrites bullets for a posting and exports with pandoc, and resume-tailor on GitHub turns your résumé and one job description into a .docx file without inventing facts. Resume Assistant, the most-downloaded résumé skill we found on ClawHub, also tailors to a job description and scores your résumé. None of them applies for you. Tsenta tailors your résumé for each role as part of applying, in Honest or Aggressive mode, through its MCP server rather than a skill.


### Does OpenClaw have an official job search skill?


No, we found no official OpenClaw job search skill on ClawHub. OpenClaw’s official plugins there include one for Indeed, which wraps Indeed’s own MCP server to search Indeed listings and does not apply. Every job skill in this guide is a community listing.


### How do I connect Tsenta to OpenClaw?


Tsenta connects to OpenClaw as an MCP server rather than a skill. OpenClaw’s docs describe saving a remote server with the streamable-http transport and OAuth, then signing in with openclaw mcp login, so use Tsenta’s server address,[https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp](https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp) , there. Tsenta does not publish a step-by-step OpenClaw guide yet, so check the tools OpenClaw lists after you sign in. Your first 25 applications are free, with no card.
